record.original_question: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated as a topological group, must K be ample?

evidence.quote: The following question occurs as a conjecture in [JK10]:
Question III. Is every infinite field K with finitely generated absolute Galois group GK ample?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a field $K$ ample (also known as large) if every smooth geometrically irreducible $K$-curve that has at least one $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points; equivalently, $K$ is existentially closed in the Laurent series field $K((t))$. Let $G_K = \mathrm{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)$ denote the absolute Galois group of $K$, regarded as a profinite (topological) group.

Question: Let $K$ be an infinite field whose absolute Galois group $G_K$ is finitely generated as a topological group. Must $K$ be ample?
artifact.category_tag: Absolute Galois groups and ample fields
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the Junker–Koenigsmann conjecture. It remains open in full generality. Partial progress includes the genus 1 case (every pointed non-singular genus 1 curve over such a K has infinitely many K-points, via elliptic curve arguments) and related results of Fehm–Petersen on infinite rank of abelian varieties over ample fields. The higher-genus and general cases are unresolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Elliptic curves and finitely generated Galois groups
status_evidence.snippet: the Junker-Koenigsmann conjecture asserts that every characteristic zero field K with finitely generated Galois group is ample ... we prove the genus 1 case
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in general; only the genus 1 case has been established.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in the Theory of Ample Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Question III. Is every infinite field K with finitely generated absolute Galois group G_K ample?
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems on ample fields.
